Overview

Update the SearchUser API endpoint (/src/Action/V1/Search/searchUser.go) to return total_post, total_follower, and a list of up to 4 recent posts (with slug and thumbnail) for each user in the search results.

Required Changes

1. Update SearchUser Model

Update the SearchUser struct in src/Models/SearchModel.go to include the new fields. We also need to define a new SearchUserPost struct to hold the thumbnail data.

// src/Models/SearchModel.go
type SearchUser struct {
	ID            string           `json:"-" gorm:"column:id"`
	Fullname      string           `json:"fullname"`
	Username      string           `json:"username"`
	Avatar        string           `json:"avatar"`
	Encrypt       string           `json:"-"`
	TotalPost     int64            `json:"total_post" gorm:"column:total_posts"`
	TotalFollower int64            `json:"total_follower" gorm:"column:total_followers"`
	Posts         []SearchUserPost `json:"posts" gorm:"-"`
}

type SearchUserPost struct {
	Slug      string `json:"slug"`
	Thumbnail string `json:"thumbnail"`
}

2. Update the Database Query

In src/Action/V1/Search/searchUser.go, update the followers_counts query to select id, total_followers, encrypt and total_posts_public (by joining views_total_posts_per_user). Ensure we use table prefixes (e.g., followers_counts.) so there's no ambiguity in the query.

// src/Action/V1/Search/searchUser.go
	var rowSearchUser []Models.SearchUser = []Models.SearchUser{}
	query := Config.DB.Table("followers_counts").
		Select("followers_counts.id, followers_counts.fullname, followers_counts.username, followers_counts.avatar, followers_counts.total_followers, followers_counts.encrypt, COALESCE(v.total_posts_public, 0) AS total_posts").
		Joins("LEFT JOIN views_total_posts_per_user v ON v.user_id = followers_counts.id").
		Where("(followers_counts.username ILIKE ? OR followers_counts.fullname ILIKE ?)", "%"+search+"%", "%"+search+"%").
		Where("followers_counts.banned = ?", false)

	// FILTER BLOCKED USER AND DEACTIVATED USER
	if len(notInEncrypt) != 0 {
		query.Where("followers_counts.encrypt NOT IN (?)", notInEncrypt)
	}

	query.Order("followers_counts.total_followers DESC, followers_counts.encrypt ASC").
		Limit(limit).
		Offset(offset).
		Scan(&rowSearchUser)

3. Fetch 4 Posts per User

After the users are retrieved into rowSearchUser, we need to loop through the results and fetch up to 4 recent public posts for each user. This query will extract slug and thumbnail directly from the posts table for optimal performance, filtering out incomplete posts.

// src/Action/V1/Search/searchUser.go
	for i := range rowSearchUser {
		var userPosts []Models.SearchUserPost
		Config.DB.Table("posts").
			Select("slug, thumbnail").
			Where("user_id = ?", rowSearchUser[i].ID).
			Where("visibility = ?", "public").
			Where("post_type != ?", "video360").
			Where("is_publish = ?", true).
			Order("created_at DESC").
			Limit(4).
			Scan(&userPosts)
		
		// Guarantee array structure instead of null if 0 posts
		if userPosts == nil {
			userPosts = []Models.SearchUserPost{}
		}
		rowSearchUser[i].Posts = userPosts
	}

Review

This is purely a GET mutation and doesn't require adding any entries to docs/EXTERNAL_MUTATIONS.md.
The views_total_posts_per_user view provides a fast way to obtain accurate post counts, and retrieving up to 4 thumbnails inside the loop uses small, indexed limits (which executes extremely fast on standard postgres).

RESULT 06/07/26

✅ Implementation: Update SQL View views_hashtag

Overview

This document outlines the implementation of the database view update for views_hashtag.
The modification ensures that post thumbnails are fetched efficiently from the database without requiring additional JOIN statements in the backend Go code.

Changes Applied

  1. Database DDL Execution: The DDL script was executed on the PostgreSQL database to recreate the views_hashtag view, selecting the p.thumbnail column from the posts table.
  2. Project Documentation: The DDL command was appended to docs/EXTERNAL_MUTATIONS.md for reference by other developers and deployment tracking.

DDL Script

-- DDL untuk memperbarui view views_hashtag
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_hashtag
AS SELECT h.tag, p.slug, u.encrypt, p.category_id, p.thumbnail 
FROM panorra_dev.public.hashtag AS h 
JOIN panorra_dev.public.posts AS p ON h.post_id = p.id 
JOIN panorra_dev.public.users AS u ON h.user_id = u.id 
WHERE (((p.visibility = 'public') AND (p.is_publish = true)) AND (p.banned = false)) AND (u.banned = false);

Side Effects

  • Simplifies queries in src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtag.go.
  • Shifts filtering logic (is_publish, visibility, banned) strictly to the database view level for optimized retrieval.

Overview

Update the database view views_hashtag to explicitly include the thumbnail column from the posts table. This allows the API to fetch thumbnails alongside tags without having to manually perform heavy JOINs on the Go application level.

Required DDL Statement

Run the following SQL in your DBMS to apply the change:

-- DDL untuk memperbarui view views_hashtag
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_hashtag
AS SELECT h.tag, p.slug, u.encrypt, p.category_id, p.thumbnail 
FROM panorra_dev.public.hashtag AS h 
JOIN panorra_dev.public.posts AS p ON h.post_id = p.id 
JOIN panorra_dev.public.users AS u ON h.user_id = u.id 
WHERE (((p.visibility = 'public') AND (p.is_publish = true)) AND (p.banned = false)) AND (u.banned = false);

Considerations

This change prevents the Go backend from explicitly checking p.visibility, is_publish, or banned status manually for thumbnails, effectively centralizing the filtering business logic on the database view.
